items.title: Omnipod 6 Coming — Expanding AID to Type 2 Diabetes
items.summary: HCPLive published a deep dive on upcoming Omnipod technology upgrades. Omnipod 6 is being designed for both Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes, expanding automated insulin delivery to the massive population of insulin-requiring T2D patients who've had limited access to pump therapy. This is the biggest expansion of AID applicability since Omnipod 5 launched. Details on timeline and specific feature improvements are still emerging from Insulet.
items.relevance: You're on Omnipod 5 right now — this is your next upgrade path. Omnipod 6 expanding to T2D is also a massive market signal: the AID ecosystem is growing, which means more mainstream awareness and potentially better insurance coverage. For AVA, a bigger AID user base means a larger audience for diabetes education tools. Worth tracking the timeline closely.

items.title: Claude Code UI Controversy — Anthropic Hides File Names, Devs Push Back Hard
items.summary: Anthropic updated Claude Code (v2.1.20+) to collapse progress output, hiding which files are being read/written behind a 'Read 3 files (ctrl+o to expand)' summary. Developers revolted on GitHub and Hacker News, arguing they need file visibility for security, catching wrong-context mistakes, and controlling token spend. Boris Cherny (Claude Code lead) initially defended it as 'reducing noise' but eventually repurposed verbose mode to show file paths as a compromise. The debate continues — many feel the compromise still removes too much info.
items.relevance: Directly affects your daily workflow with Claude Code. If you update to the latest version, file read/write names will be hidden by default. Enable verbose mode in settings to get them back. The broader signal: Anthropic is optimizing Claude Code for longer agentic runs where output volume gets overwhelming — but power users want the details. Keep verbose mode on.

items.title: Anthropic vs. The Pentagon — $200M Contract at Risk Over Military AI Usage Limits
items.summary: The Pentagon is pressuring AI companies (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI) to allow military use of their AI for 'all lawful purposes.' Anthropic is the most resistant, drawing a hard line against fully autonomous weapons and mass domestic surveillance. The Pentagon is threatening to pull its $200M contract. One unnamed company has already agreed to the terms. Claude was reportedly used in the U.S. military operation to capture Venezuela's Maduro, adding fuel to the debate.
items.relevance: Anthropic makes the AI you use daily. Their willingness to push back on military usage — even at the cost of $200M — says something about the company's values and long-term direction. From a practical standpoint, Anthropic walking away from defense money could mean more pressure to grow commercial revenue, which could affect pricing or features for developers like you.

items.title: China's AI Video & Robotics Wave — Seedance 2.0, Kling 3.0, RynnBrain
items.summary: Chinese tech giants dropped major AI models this week. ByteDance released Seedance 2.0 (realistic AI video generation from text/image prompts), Kuaishou launched Kling 3.0 (competing directly with OpenAI's Sora), and Alibaba's DAMO Academy unveiled RynnBrain — a robotics AI model that gives robots spatial and temporal awareness to perform complex physical tasks. Google DeepMind's CEO said Chinese models are now just 'months' behind Western rivals.
items.relevance: The video generation models (Seedance 2.0, Kling 3.0) could be useful for creating AVA marketing content — realistic AI-generated demo videos without needing to hire videographers. RynnBrain's robotics approach is more long-term interesting. The competitive pressure from China keeps pushing all AI labs to ship faster, which benefits end users.

items.title: AI Dev Tool Power Rankings — Claude Code Holds Strong, Antigravity Disrupts
items.summary: LogRocket's February 2026 AI dev tool rankings compared 12 tools and 15 models. Windsurf (formerly Codeium) took #1 with its Cascade AI agent and live preview. Antigravity (free, multi-agent orchestration with built-in Chrome automation) landed #2. Claude Code maintained a top position for its deep codebase understanding and agentic workflow capabilities. The rankings now track Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, and newcomer Kimi K2.5 among models.
items.relevance: Good benchmark for where Claude Code sits vs. competition. Antigravity is the interesting newcomer — free with multi-agent orchestration and browser automation (similar to what Clawdbot does). Windsurf's Cascade agent is worth watching. But for your workflow (CLI-based, deep codebase work, sub-agent spawning), Claude Code + Clawdbot is still the most flexible setup.

items.title: Medtronic Simplera CGM Approved + Abbott Partnership Expands AID Access
items.summary: FDA approved Medtronic's Simplera CGM — a smaller, tape-free, simplified-insertion glucose monitor. Simultaneously, Medtronic announced a global partnership with Abbott: Abbott will provide its advanced CGM platform exclusively integrated into Medtronic's insulin delivery and Smart MDI systems. This means Medtronic pumps will work with both Simplera and Abbott-based CGMs, giving users more sensor options within one ecosystem.
items.relevance: The Medtronic-Abbott partnership is a big deal for the CGM landscape. More sensor options = more competition = potentially lower costs. The tape-free design on Simplera addresses one of the biggest user complaints (skin irritation from overtape). Kaislyn is on Tandem + Dexcom so this doesn't directly affect her setup, but it signals the whole industry is racing to make CGMs smaller and more comfortable — which is great for all T1D kids.

items.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark on Cerebras Hardware — Latency-First AI Coding
items.summary: OpenAI partnered with Cerebras to run a new GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark model on Cerebras' Wafer Scale Engine 3, a purpose-built AI accelerator optimized for ultra-low latency inference. The model runs in the same production stack as other OpenAI models but with a dedicated fast-inference tier. The focus is on discovering what near-instant AI coding responses enable — new interaction patterns and use cases that aren't possible with standard latency.
items.relevance: OpenAI is betting that dramatically faster inference changes how developers interact with AI coding tools — not just faster responses, but fundamentally different workflows when latency drops below human reaction time. This competitive pressure benefits you regardless of which tool you use: Anthropic will need to match on speed. For now, Claude Code's depth still beats raw speed for complex projects.
